description: We are a team of developers and innovators in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge building real-time health-monitoring tools to safeguard astronauts against radiation, isolation, and microgravity risks during long-duration space missions.
summary:
ASTRA is a web-based astronaut health monitoring system that tracks heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO2), and body temperature on a centralized dashboard. It visualizes health trends, compares readings against personal baselines, and uses rule-based detection to generate alerts for unusual patterns.
​In extreme space environments, ASTRA makes biometric data easy to interpret so potential concerns are spotted early. Timely monitoring supports faster decision-making, proactive care, and safer missions.

​Note: This website is a prototype created strictly for demonstration purposes, and Netlify was used to create its public domain.
details: ASTRA – Astronaut Health Monitoring and Early-Warning System ASTRA is a proposed health-monitoring software system designed to support astronauts during space missions by monitoring their physical health indicators and identifying unusual changes that may require attention. Astronauts in space face several health challenges, including cardiovascular changes, muscle and bone loss, sleep disturbances, fatigue and psychological stress. Monitoring these changes is important, particularly during long-duration missions where access to immediate medical assistance may be limited. How does ASTRA work? ASTRA provides a centralized dashboard that displays important health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature and wellness information. It uses health readings and individual baseline values to identify unusual patterns. The system analyzes incoming readings using a rule-based anomaly detection mechanism and categorizes health status into normal, warning and critical levels. When an unusual pattern is detected, it generates an alert explaining the observed change and provides predefined recommendations, such as repeating a measurement or following the appropriate mission medical protocol. The application also provides historical health graphs to help astronauts and mission control understand changes in health over time. The initial prototype will use simulated astronaut health data to demonstrate its monitoring and alert-generation capabilities. Benefits and Intended Impact - Helps astronauts keep track of important health indicators. - Identifies unusual health patterns through continuous analysis of available readings. - Makes health trends easier to understand through visual dashboards and graphs. - Provides timely alerts to support awareness and decision-making. - Can help mission control review astronaut health information when communication is available. - Provides a foundation for future integration with wearable health sensors and offline-first monitoring systems. Technology and Tools The proposed implementation uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the user interface, Chart.js for data visualization, and JavaScript-based rules for health-pattern detection. Local storage or a database can be used to maintain health history. Simulated sensor data will be used for the initial demonstration. Creativity and Innovation ASTRA focuses on more than displaying individual health measurements. Its key idea is to compare readings against an astronaut's personal health baseline and highlight unusual or sustained changes. Instead of presenting only numerical values, it explains why an alert was generated and suggests an appropriate next step. The system is designed with future offline operation and integration with real wearable sensors in mind, making it adaptable to the communication and resource constraints of space missions. Project Considerations and Limitations The prototype considers the need for reliable data handling, understandable alerts, individual health differences, limited connectivity and the importance of astronaut safety. It is intended as a health-monitoring and decision-support prototype, not a medical diagnostic system. All health recommendations must remain subject to approved mission medical procedures and qualified medical supervision. Our long-term vision is to develop ASTRA into an intelligent astronaut health-monitoring platform that supports safer and more informed human space exploration.
